summary: Interpreted the retained execution and filed the defect account, then submitted a corrected successor run. The retained receipt (CheckRun 3fea35115a164e10bd378355a297b42f, exit 0, cases A/B/C passed) shows the false completion end to end: with the leader partitioned and its entry accepted only locally, node 3 decided a different entry at the same index, and the origin's `append_notify` resolved `Ok(assigned_idx=1)` while the decided log at index 1 held `22` and the caller's entry `11` appeared in no decided log — whereas the same call without a partition resolved `Ok` with the entry actually present, and the identical lost-entry setup with 2 ms ticks resolved the documented `Superseded`. So the appended Interpretation asserts the scoped defect (`violated`/`asserted`), answers the registered gap as reachable-and-observed, and a new knowledge entry records the measured schedule dependence with the receipt indices. The v1 comparison machinery returned `unknown` only because my admission events lacked the identity fields, so the witness here rests on the receipt's parsed events; the successor experiment (same cases and comparisons, admission events now carrying origin/submitted_value) was submitted to make the comparison chain evaluable. Incomplete: that successor receipt is pending, and the caller-facing consequence (whether any in-repo consumer treats `Ok` as a durable-write signal) is still open.
